THE DIVERGENCE WORTH NOTING, AND ITS LIMIT
  The UK is today's outlier among the three bond markets we track: the gilt yield ROSE about four
  basis points while the French ten-year EASED and the US ten-year sits around 5% — and this is five
  days before the Budget on Wednesday 28 October. That is a factual contrast and is reported as one.
  NO APPROVED SOURCE READ SO FAR ATTRIBUTES THE GILT MOVE TO THE BUDGET OR TO ANYTHING ELSE, so no
  cause is asserted for it.

CONTINUITY WITH OUR OWN PUBLISHED SERIES (22 Oct morning, 11:25)
  Gilt   published 5.37 -> 5.37 today (prev close 5.3299; up 4bp today). Consistent.
  UST    published 5.07 -> 4.99 today. Note both facts are true and must not be conflated: the level
         has FALLEN about 8bp since our last edition, but it is UP about 4bp on the day against
         today's previous close of 4.953. The ticker change field carries today's move.
  Gold   published 4,091.58 -> 4,003.53. A continued fall of roughly 2% since our last edition, on
         top of the 1.2% fall we reported then.
  Brent  published 111.99 -> 116.13. Up roughly $4 since our last edition.
  No value is carried forward; every figure is a fresh read.

NOTE ON THIS EDITION: no evening edition was published on 22 October and no morning edition on
23 October, because the scheduled job failed four times across eleven hours. This is therefore the
first market reading published on the site since 22 October at 11:25, which is why the continuity
section above spans two days rather than one.

OIL, VERIFIED AGAINST THE ARTICLE RATHER THAN THE FILENAME
  The cached file is named "cnbc-oil-brent-five-month-high-iran.txt" by the failed automated run.
  THE ARTICLE SAYS SIX-MONTH: "Brent crude oil was trading at a six-month high on Friday ... the
  highest level since April 30." Published 11:51 BST. At that time it had Brent +2% at $115.41 and
  WTI +2.4% at $101.86. Our own 15:57 read is $116.13, +2.62%, so the move extended through the
  afternoon; the LEVEL we publish is our own read and the "six-month high since 30 April" framing is
  CNBC's. CNBC attributes the move to investors increasingly expecting the United States to resume
  strikes on Iran in the coming weeks.
  *** This is the second time in two days that a cache FILENAME written by the automated job has
  carried a wrong figure. Never take a number from a filename; open the file. ***
